evidence.location: section 4, RP2 row, line 241; against section 2 RP2, lines 182-186, and section 5, lines 258-262
evidence.observation: Line 241 reads "**RP2-C4** a textual rule's line is unchanged.", but lines 184-185 read "The report line changes from the hard-coded `textual rule:` text to the row's reason" with "the textual row's reason is its expression" (line 182), and lines 259-261 read "changes only where RP2's report line changes (`textual rule:` → the row's reason)". The hard-coded string exists at src/gnd/export/pyrel_rules.py:1648 (print(f"{rule['id']}  not checked  (textual rule: {rule['expression']})")), so the textual line's prefix is removed by the very design RP2 describes. RP2 cannot be tested as written: satisfying RP2-C4 fails the section 2/5 behaviour and vice versa.

concerns.recommendation: Before the RP2 spec gate, reword RP2-C4 to state the intended invariant once: either pin the new textual line (id, not checked, the expression as reason) or assert textual rules are still listed on every run, counted in the success line and exit-banded, so sections 2, 4 and 5 agree.
concerns.title: RP2-C4 says a textual rule's line is unchanged while sections 2 and 5 change it

evidence.location: section 2 RP1, lines 156-159 and 163-164; section 4, RP1-C6, line 240
evidence.observation: Lines 157-158 bind "the anchor roles bound to per-copy variables keyed by object type (`$<object type>_1`, `$<object type>_2`)" and lines 163-164 refuse only "A join that GND would refuse as disconnected". But _require_joinable (src/gnd/checker/_core.py:1156-1184) raises two refusals: JoinDisconnectedError and JoinAmbiguousError at lines 1182-1184 when one referenced fact type has more than one anchor role of the same object type. In that case the keyed-variable scheme gives both anchor roles the same per-copy variable, silently forcing them equal and compiling a requirement GND declines to evaluate, against section 0's "A program that enforces more than GND checks is a defect too". RP1-C6 (line 240) covers only the disconnected refusal ("a disconnected external join is refused by name").

concerns.recommendation: Mirror both _require_joinable refusals in RP1: refuse ambiguous external joins by name before lowering, and extend RP1-C6 (or add a criterion) so the ambiguity refusal is tested alongside the disconnection one.
concerns.title: RP1 refuses disconnected external joins but not the ambiguous joins _require_joinable also refuses

evidence.location: section 2 RP1, lines 159-160; section 4, RP1-C3, line 240
evidence.observation: Lines 159-160 state the check as "The check is `same` over the anchor pairs: two joined rows with equal referenced values must have equal anchors", but GND's verdict (src/gnd/semantic_spec.py:1065-1085, uniqueness_result) marks any joined referenced-value tuple counted twice as violated regardless of anchors, and _join_rows matches anchors by _identity_key. Two joined rows whose referenced values and anchors are identity-equal but textually distinct (e.g. 1 and 1.0 in a Number role, which RP3 makes loadable; not an exact JSON duplicate, so neither the programs' repeated-fact refusal nor the oracle test's exact-duplicate dedup at tests/test_pyrel_rules.py:110-117 removes it) violate in gnd check and pass the `same` check. RP1-C3's three cases (exit 0, one duplicate with a witness, empty join) do not cover this boundary.

concerns.recommendation: Add an RP1-C3 oracle case for a repeat whose anchors are identity-equal (or a numeric-encoding pair that GND's identity joins), or state the equality-vs-identity boundary on the runtime page as a difference, the way D4 does for String.
concerns.title: RP1's same-over-anchor-pairs check passes repeats with identity-equal anchors that gnd check reports as violations

summary: Digest verified. Read the plan against src/gnd/export/pyrel_rules.py, src/gnd/checker/_core.py, src/gnd/semantic_spec.py, src/gnd/constraint_families.py, src/gnd/export/pyrel_runtime.py, the cited tests, docs pages and the packaged literature examples at this checkout. The section 1 refusal table, code citations, measured GND behaviour and the D1-D5 rulings match the repository; the RP1 lowering is the same object-type-keyed shared-entity join _join_rows uses, with empty-join vacuity as _JOIN_SUBJECT_SEQS decides it, and the RP3/RP4 lowerings agree with the checker's Number identity and role-scoped vacuity. One blocking contradiction inside RP2 (criterion RP2-C4 vs sections 2 and 5 on the textual not-checked line), one missing ambiguity refusal and one identity-boundary case for RP1's join, and two low completeness nicks.
